newsitem.title: USA: Arbitrage attracts Brent crude to U.S.. [CORRECTED 23:01 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Arbitrage attracts Brent crude to U.S.. [CORRECTED 23:01 GMT]

text.p: The wide transatlantic arbitrage drew continued offers for North Sea Brent crude oil into the U.S. Gulf Coast on Tuesday, traders said.

A U.S. company fixed a VLCC of Brent for loading around May 10. One cargo was sold to a Gulf Coast refiner for a discount of 80 cents to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on a delivered basis.
The seller was expected to retain two more of the cargoes for its own refining system, leaving one available at WTI minus 77 cents a barrel delivered.
A U.S. major was heard to be still trying to resell a Brent for May 8-10 arrival, asking WTI minus 80 cents a barrel.
"They're going to have a hard time moving that one," one trader said of the offer. "Everyone's done for that time frame. There isn't any prompt demand....The arb's good enough, it's all timing."
A Swiss trader was also showing Brent for June 10-15 arrival, asking WTI minus 75-80 cents a barrel delivered.
From West Africa, a U.S. equity producer was offering a Nigerian Qua Iboe cargo for June 18-23, asking dated Brent plus $1.90 a barrel on a delivered basis.
A European company was offering Nigerian Bonny Light into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) at 37 cents below WTI (corrects from "at about parity with WTI"), traders said.
In Latin America, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP bought one million barrels of Iranian Light crude oil from Brazil's state oil company Petrobras in its latest crude tender, trade sources said.
The crude will be delivered to Uruguay's Jose Ignacio terminal in the second half of June.
The price was related to dated Brent, the sources said.

From Venezuela, state Petroleos de Venezuela was heard offering Mesa-30 crude for June at a discount of $3.00 to WTI, a level much firmer than May, partly as a result of softening Caribbean freight rates and higher sour crude prices, traders said.
"The Venezuelans have stopped their firesale...their surplus is gone," a trader said.
From Colombia, eight Cusiana cargoes are on tap for June loading, traders said.
State Ecopetrol is tendering South Blend and Cano Limon cargoes for June 20-30 and June 13-23, respectively. Two Cusiana cargoes are being tendered, traders said.
